items.title: Cross-surface consumer ownership is explicit
items.statement: The reviewed window explicitly assigns editor semantic affordances, text search, aggregated diagnostics, and degraded-capability disclosure to distinct consumers, preventing a second owner from being implied for these surfaces.

evidence.exact_quote: - File Manager and editor consume LSP state for semantic affordances
- Search remains the owner of text search and replace-in-files
- Problems remains the owner of aggregated diagnostics display
- status surfaces disclose freshness, health, and effective capability state rather than hiding degraded attach conditions

items.title: Requested and effective GUI state are separated
items.statement: The Settings contract explicitly distinguishes requested state from effective runtime attachment and enumerates masked, missing, misconfigured, unavailable, override, and provenance states.

evidence.exact_quote: - `Settings > LSP lists all servers and custom entries with validation`; that phrase is a product requirement, not a placeholder. The GUI includes a global master toggle, a searchable `/filterable` full-catalog list, per-server enable/disable, add custom server `/form`, edit custom server action, `/built-in` override/reset behavior, malformed command/config validation, visible distinction among catalog/built-in server, built-in server with user override, user-added custom server, disabled/enabled/misconfigured/unavailable states, command plus args, handled extensions/selectors, env/init options, root-discovery mode, install `/provisioning` notes, and global vs project-scope override. Requested state and effective state must both be shown when a global enablement is masked by a project override or missing binary.

items.title: Remote disconnect recovery is explicit
items.statement: The authorized context immediately following the core supplies a concrete degraded transition, reconnect behavior, reinitialization, and a safety condition for request replay, so remote network loss is not wholly unspecified in this window.

evidence.exact_quote: - if SSH disconnects, all remote LSP servers on that connection are marked `degraded`, reconnect is attempted, servers are re-initialized, and pending requests are replayed when safe

items.title: Startup completion has no generation guard
items.statement: The required registration-before-spawn sequence defines starting, ready, and failed, but it does not require a generation token or identity recheck before a late handshake mutates the map. A concurrent disable, restart, root removal, or replacement can therefore be overwritten by the old startup task.

evidence.exact_quote: Any asynchronous LSP startup goroutine or background initialization task is lifecycle-tracked BEFORE spawn: it must register a cancellable `lifecycle-tracker` handle before subprocess creation or watcher launch, and failed handshakes must either mark the existing record `failed` or tear the handle down.
5. Transition the record to `ready` or `failed` after handshake completion.

items.impact: A stale process can become authoritative after the user disabled it or after a newer session took its key, leaking responses and leaving shutdown ownership ambiguous.
items.builder_discretion: Specify a monotonically increasing session generation or unique instance token checked under the map lock for every startup completion and exit callback.

items.title: Debounced document sync lacks flush and ordering barriers
items.statement: The didChange rule resets a debounce timer and emits later, but the reviewed window does not say that pending changes must flush before didSave, didClose, rename, format, navigation, or a version-sensitive semantic request. The server may observe an older buffer or receive lifecycle notifications out of order.

evidence.exact_quote: | **didChange flood** | **Client:** Debounce `didChange` (default 100 ms after last edit; §7, §14.4). When server supports incremental sync, send only `contentChanges`; otherwise full content. **When:** On every buffer edit, start/reset debounce timer; on timer fire, send one `didChange`. |

items.impact: Hover, rename, formatting, diagnostics, or save-triggered server work can target stale text, and the final edit can be lost to the server on close.
items.builder_discretion: Define a serialized per-document notification queue and mandatory flush/cancel barriers for save, close, and operations that consume the current document version.

items.title: Workspace edit partial failure and rollback are not specified
items.statement: Rename and code actions are approval-gated and routed through FileSafe, but this window does not define preflight, atomicity, per-file conflict handling, rollback, retry, or the user-visible result when only part of a multi-file workspace edit applies.

evidence.exact_quote: Diagnostic-to-chat pipeline behavior is a context-packaging contract, not a second diagnostics owner. The `to-chat` payload uses the same diagnostic entry shape as §17.2 (`path`, `line`, `character`, `severity`, `message`, `source`, optional `code`) plus refs to the originating LSP session and URI; severity mapping preserves `Error`, `Warning`, `Info`, and `Hint` labels when chat summarizes or filters diagnostics. Chat LSP remains read-only for MVP; when a separate later-phase chat workflow surfaces a quick fix, code action, rename, or workspace edit from this diagnostic context, it opens explicit preview/confirmation and applies only through FileSafe-backed `workspace/applyEdit`, preserving the code action approval flow rather than mutating directly from the message.
- [ ] Code actions: textDocument/codeAction; context menu/lightbulb; apply via workspace/applyEdit (FileSafe).

items.impact: A failed rename can leave a workspace internally inconsistent while the GUI reports only that the approved action ran.
items.builder_discretion: Bind this plan to an explicit FileSafe transaction result envelope covering preflight conflicts, all-or-nothing capability, compensation, and per-file failure disclosure.

items.title: Custom server execution trust boundary is absent
items.statement: The GUI accepts custom commands, arguments, environment, initialization options, and overrides, yet the reviewed window specifies only malformed-config validation. It does not define executable trust prompts, command-path resolution, working directory, environment inheritance/redaction, sandboxing, or project-vs-global authority.

evidence.exact_quote: - [ ] Per-server enable/disable: honor lsp.<id>.disabled and lsp: false. **GUI:** Settings > LSP: all built-in servers listed with Enable toggle (default on); user can turn any off. Global "Disable automatic LSP server downloads" toggle; per-server env and initialization options; custom LSP servers (add/edit/remove: command, extensions, env, initialization). See FinalGUISpec §7.4.2.

items.impact: A repository or lower-scope override could cause arbitrary local or remote command execution or expose inherited credentials when a matching file opens.
items.builder_discretion: Define configuration provenance, trust elevation, scope precedence, executable resolution, minimal environment, secret handling, and confirmation requirements before spawn.

items.title: Server-authored presentation content is not treated as untrusted
items.statement: Diagnostics, hover, completion, code lenses, document links, and code actions originate in external server processes and flow into GUI or chat, but this window contains no sanitization, URI-scheme allowlist, markup policy, command allowlist, or size limit for those payloads.

evidence.exact_quote: - [ ] **Additional enhancements (§9.1):** textDocument/formatting (format document/selection); textDocument/documentLink (clickable imports); optional: LSP diagnostics verification gate, LSP snapshot in evidence, Chat "Fix all" / "Rename" / "Where is this used?" / "Format file"; promote lsp tool when ready.

items.impact: A malicious or compromised language server can create spoofed UI, unsafe links, oversized payload denial of service, or unauthorized command execution paths.
items.builder_discretion: Specify rendering sanitization, safe URI schemes, resource bounds, command registration/approval, and rejection telemetry for all server-authored fields.

items.title: Chat virtual-document data lifecycle is unspecified
items.statement: Non-file chat code blocks are sent through a virtual-document contract, but this window does not define consent, URI isolation, content retention, didClose timing, diagnostic cleanup, workspace association, or whether custom/remote servers may receive private chat text.

evidence.exact_quote: - code blocks that map to project files use those real file URIs; other code blocks use the virtual-document contract in §14.8

items.impact: Sensitive chat-only code may persist in a server, be attributed to the wrong project, or cross a host boundary without a visible disclosure.
items.builder_discretion: Make the virtual-document contract specify per-thread opaque URIs, server eligibility, disclosure/consent, lifecycle close and purge, and diagnostic teardown.

items.title: Accessibility behavior is absent from the dense Settings surface
items.statement: The registry defines search, filters, toggles, badges, forms, actions, and detail panes, but the reviewed window provides no keyboard order, focus restoration, accessible names, state announcements, non-color encoding, or error association requirements.

evidence.exact_quote: - The LSP registry participates in the GUI Settings `/inspectors` pattern and the `two-level` Settings navigation model. Registry `/filtering` and `/filter/grouping` cover at least `/ecosystem`, language, source, requested state, effective state, support classification, and lifecycle state. Detail panes show canonical `/names`, aliases/source names, `/install/download/legal` and `/provisioning` posture, platform restrictions, command/env/init fields, and validation errors without turning Settings into the SSOT for runtime attachment.

items.impact: Keyboard-only and assistive-technology users may be unable to discover effective state, correct validation errors, or safely invoke reset/remove actions.
items.builder_discretion: Add testable keyboard, focus, announcement, naming, contrast/non-color, and validation-linkage requirements for registry and status surfaces.

items.title: User-visible strings and status vocabulary have no localization contract
items.statement: The window mandates literal English status and action copy but does not identify localization keys, parameterized messages, plural rules, truncation behavior, or whether protocol/server strings are translated versus preserved.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Server crash or exit** | **Client (LSP layer):** On process exit or broken pipe (e.g. when writing to stdin fails), (1) mark that server's state as Error, (2) clear all diagnostics for documents owned by that server (DiagnosticsCache), (3) notify UI to refresh Problems panel and gutter. **UI:** Show "Error" in status bar for that server; offer "Restart language server" button (or auto-restart with exponential backoff, e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s, cap 30s). **Logging:** Log exit code and stderr tail for debugging. |

items.impact: Translations may diverge across status bar, Problems, chat, and Settings or overflow fixed layouts, while raw server text is inconsistently localized.
items.builder_discretion: Define stable message keys, variables, ownership of server-supplied text, and layout/assistive tests under expansion and RTL locales.

items.title: Workspace and document caps have no deterministic overflow policy
items.statement: The plan caps initialization roots and suggests document caps, but does not define root selection when more than ten roots are active, eviction ordering, pinning, reactivation, starvation prevention, or how reduced coverage is disclosed.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Many open documents** | **Client:** Limit documents pushed to each server (e.g. only currently open tabs, or N most recent per root). **Editor/FileManager:** When a buffer is evicted (FileManager §12.2.1), **client** sends `didClose` for that URI so the server can free memory. **Config:** Optional cap (e.g. max 50 open docs per server) in Settings. |

| **Large workspace at init** | **Client:** At initialize, send only roots that have at least one open document, capped at 10 (§7, §14.6). **When:** During `initialize` request; do not send thousands of paths. |

items.impact: Valid files or roots can silently lose diagnostics and semantic features, with behavior depending on nondeterministic open order.
items.builder_discretion: Specify deterministic per-root quotas and recency rules, protected active/dirty buffers, dynamic workspace-folder behavior, and visible coverage counters.

items.title: Compatibility removals lack persisted-state migration
items.statement: The plan deprecates or removes legacy widget layout identifiers and treats lsp_rename as an alias, but the reviewed window does not define migration of persisted layouts, saved commands, API callers, config versions, or downgrade behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - Widget layout compatibility is narrow: keep `widget_layout:v1:dashboard`, `widget_layout:v1:usage`, and `widget_layout:v1:orchestrator:progress`; deprecate or remove `widget_layout:v1:orchestrator:tiers`, `widget_layout:v1:orchestrator:evidence`, `widget_layout:v1:orchestrator:history`, and `widget_layout:v1:orchestrator:ledger` when LSP-facing Orchestrator surfaces project progress or diagnostics.

- LSP canon must preserve the exact MVP operation inventory, normalized parameter shapes, and result envelope. The canonical tool surface is nine read-only operations plus one write/approval-gated `rename`; the packetization label `10 read-only + 1 write-gated (lsp_rename)` is reconciled here by treating `lsp_rename` as a legacy alias for `rename`, not a second operation. `workspaceSymbol` must carry `query`, position-based operations use `path` + `position`, and `rename` / `lsp_rename` requires `path` + `position` + `newName` with approval gating.

items.impact: Existing users or callers can lose layouts or fail calls even though the prose describes the old vocabulary as compatible.
items.builder_discretion: Define read-old/write-new migrations, alias lifetime and telemetry, collision behavior, downgrade compatibility, and migration tests.

items.title: Crash observability can leak secrets and lacks correlation
items.statement: The only concrete crash support data in this window is exit code and stderr tail. No redaction, byte cap, retention, session/root correlation, restart-attempt counter, diagnostic-clear reason, or support-export contract is defined.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Server crash or exit** | **Client (LSP layer):** On process exit or broken pipe (e.g. when writing to stdin fails), (1) mark that server's state as Error, (2) clear all diagnostics for documents owned by that server (DiagnosticsCache), (3) notify UI to refresh Problems panel and gutter. **UI:** Show "Error" in status bar for that server; offer "Restart language server" button (or auto-restart with exponential backoff, e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s, cap 30s). **Logging:** Log exit code and stderr tail for debugging. |

items.impact: Support cannot reliably join a failure to the affected session or explain lost diagnostics, while stderr may persist source paths, tokens, or other secrets.
items.builder_discretion: Specify structured correlated events, bounded/redacted capture, retention, counters, user-visible diagnostics provenance, and an opt-in support export.

items.title: Destructive remove and reset actions have no safety contract
items.statement: Custom server removal, catalog reset, global disable, and worktree-triggered shutdown are exposed, but the reviewed window does not require impact preview, confirmation, pending-request cancellation, dirty virtual-document handling, undo, or recovery from a mistaken action.

evidence.exact_quote: - Registry rows expose `/languages`, `/selectors`, source badges (`Microsoft`, `OpenCode`, `PM`, `Custom`), classification badges (`Default managed`, `Manual/toolchain`, `Experimental`), `/install` and `/toolchain` provenance, explicit `/effective-state`, path and `/exclusion` controls, and built-in `Override` plus `Reset to catalog defaults` actions. Custom rows keep full edit and remove controls; built-in rows keep read-only catalog metadata except for allowed overrides.
- When the worktree is removed, the associated LSP session is shut down gracefully

items.impact: A user can silently remove effective language support or terminate a session with in-flight work and no clear restoration path.
items.builder_discretion: Define impact summaries, confirmation thresholds, graceful-drain semantics, undo/restore for configuration, and explicit post-action status.

items.title: Status bar contract does not resolve multiple concurrent sessions
items.statement: The status requirement names one server and one lifecycle label, while this same window permits multiple servers and worktrees. It does not define aggregation, active-file selection, conflicting states, hidden failures, or navigation from summary to the affected session.

evidence.exact_quote: - [ ] LSP status in UI: status bar or indicator (server name, Initializing/Ready/Error).
- Multiple worktrees may each have their own LSP session for the same server_id (each with a different root_identity)

items.impact: A healthy active session can mask a failing background session, or a global error can be mistaken for the active file's state.
items.builder_discretion: Specify active-document status plus aggregate counts/severity, stable session identity, and drill-down to project/root/server details.

items.title: Implementation checklist lacks falsifiable acceptance oracles
items.statement: The window asserts that edge cases are defined elsewhere and lists implementation outcomes, but it does not bind these requirements to named tests, fixtures, failure injection, expected event sequences, or machine-checkable result assertions within the reviewed contract.

evidence.exact_quote: **Edge cases and fallback:** For each checklist item below, success/failure behavior, edge cases (timeout, server crash, stale response), and **fallback when LSP unavailable** are defined in §1.1 (Purpose), §5 (Editor), §5.1 (Chat), §8 (mitigations), and §13 (GUI). Config keys: §14.4.

items.impact: Implementations can satisfy prose subjectively while violating ordering, stale-response, approval, fallback, or degraded-state behavior without a deterministic gate failing.
items.builder_discretion: Add acceptance matrices with initial state, stimulus, exact ordered outputs, injected failure, GUI truth, persistence effects, and pass/fail assertions for every lifecycle and operation.

items.title: Virtual-document closure cannot be established from the assigned window
items.statement: The assigned excerpt delegates non-file chat code blocks to §14.8, but that referenced section is outside this capsule. Under blind-window restrictions, whether it closes lifecycle, privacy, authority, and cleanup obligations is unknown.

evidence.exact_quote: - code blocks that map to project files use those real file URIs; other code blocks use the virtual-document contract in §14.8

items.impact: This review cannot distinguish a local omission from a contract satisfied later in the same document.
items.builder_discretion: Resolve only in a later authorized cross-window seam phase; do not infer closure from this capsule.

dimension_assessments.summary: The core names the principal editor, File Manager, Search, Problems, chat, status, Settings, Orchestrator, runtime-artifact, and AI-context consumers and separates their ownership.
Starting/ready/failed and requested/effective states exist, but stale startup completion and debounce lifecycle ordering are not closed.
Registration precedes spawn, but no generation guard prevents a late handshake or exit callback from mutating a replaced session record.
Multi-file workspace edits lack an explicit partial-apply result and recovery contract.
Crash/reconnect recovery is described, but mutation rollback and mistaken destructive-action recovery remain unspecified.
Surface ownership is clear, but custom executable provenance and scope authority are not.
Virtual chat documents and stderr capture have no complete disclosure, retention, purge, or redaction contract in the assigned window.
Custom process configuration and server-authored GUI/chat payloads cross trust boundaries without execution or rendering constraints.
Requested/effective/degraded distinctions are strong, but a single-server status-bar shape does not truthfully aggregate concurrent sessions.
The authorized context after the core explicitly covers SSH disconnect degradation, reconnect, reinitialization, safe replay, timeout multiplication, and no hidden mirror.
Caps are proposed, but deterministic selection, starvation, reactivation, and disclosure semantics are missing.
The complex registry and lifecycle status surfaces contain no testable keyboard, focus, announcement, naming, or non-color contract.
Literal English labels and protocol/server text lack localization ownership and layout rules.
Compatibility vocabulary is identified, but persisted layout, config, alias, and downgrade migrations are not.
Exit-code/stderr logging lacks redaction, correlation, retention, structured counters, and support-export behavior.
Remove, reset, disable, and worktree-triggered shutdown have no explicit confirmation, drain, undo, or restoration semantics.
The assigned core repeatedly routes ownership through named contracts and explicitly keeps Search, Problems, editor, chat, and status responsibilities distinct.
The checklist has prose outcomes and cross-references but no bound machine-checkable lifecycle and failure oracles in this window.
The blind capsule excludes referenced §14.8, so virtual-document closure cannot be established without violating the assignment boundary.
